title: Compression at the Edge — NVIDIA, Unsloth, HuggingFace, Ollama
talk_summary: A panel of NVIDIA, Unsloth, HuggingFace and Ollama engineers discuss model compression/quantization: mixed-precision layer selection, NVFP4 micro-block scaling, and how to verify a compressed model isn't degraded.

takeaways.technique: Bigger model quantized beats smaller model at native precision
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite a paper showing a 4x larger model at 4-bit outperforms a smaller model at BF16 at equal disk size, and recommend routing: big model for planning, small fast model for execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use the big ones for planning and then you execution with the small ones
takeaways.numbers: 120B at 4-bit beats 35B at 16-bit at same size; small models ~200 tok/s vs ~5-10 tok/s for compressed big model

takeaways.technique: KL-divergence as a cheap quality proxy
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of noisy accuracy benchmarks, they measure KL divergence between the quantized model's output logits and the BF16 original over calibration data, targeting near-zero distance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: KOD is the distance between the uncontized version which is Bflat 16 and your quantized version
takeaways.numbers: NVIDIA targets <1% accuracy degradation on AA benchmarks for FP4

takeaways.technique: Benchmarks don't capture harness behavior; test in the real harness
takeaways.what_they_do: They note quantized models can pass benchmarks but behave wrong in an actual agent harness, so they run the model inside the real tool (e.g. Claude Code) and judge behavior, not just scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's literally me you know running through putting it in cloud code or something and running the model it's like no it doesn't feel just right

takeaways.technique: Distill midsize models for narrow tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They mention companies distilling midsize models into very small ones for narrow jobs like reranking that don't need full LLM output, cutting millions in cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: companies that actually distill midsize models to like very small ones for like reranking or whatever

takeaways.technique: Leave small models at higher precision
takeaways.what_they_do: Ollama defaults some small models to higher precision because quantizing them too aggressively degrades usability, accepting larger size for reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we sometimes leave it in higher precision um as a default just because we actually want people to have a better experience
